problem.claim: The study asks what methods support successful production deployment of LLM-based agents and examines why and how organizations build and evaluate them.

gap.claim: Existing understanding lacks visibility into the technical methods and deployment realities associated with successful production agents.

contributions.claim: Introduces MAP, a systematic study based on first-hand data from agent developers.
Documents the current state of production agents and identifies underexplored research avenues.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe MAP as the first systematic study of measuring agents in production.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report 20 in-depth interview case studies and a survey of 86 practitioners covering 26 domains.
The authors report that 68% of production agents execute at most 10 steps before human intervention, 70% use prompting rather than weight tuning, and 74% rely primarily on human evaluation.
The authors report reliability as the top development challenge, addressed by practitioners through systems-level design.

narrative_sequence.summary: Production agents are widespread, but the methods behind successful deployments are poorly understood.
MAP investigates organizational motivations, construction methods, evaluation practices, and development challenges using interviews and a practitioner survey.
Reported deployments favor short, controllable workflows, prompting of off-the-shelf models, and human evaluation.
Reliability remains the leading challenge, while MAP exposes deployment realities and possible research directions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns deployment-characterization claims with explicit study coverage and concrete prevalence figures.

lessons.interpretation: A compact empirical framing can make an operational landscape legible when it connects sampling scope to quantified patterns.
lessons.application: State the data sources and coverage first, then attach each major deployment pattern to a clearly defined percentage and condition.
lessons.exception: Avoid percentage-based generalization when the sample, domain coverage, or denominator is not adequately described.

source_observation.claim: The study defines reliability as consistent correct behavior over time and links it to systems-level design responses.

lessons.interpretation: Defining an abstract engineering challenge and naming the current response can sharpen a research agenda.
lessons.application: Define the target property operationally and distinguish the deployment layer where practitioners currently intervene.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the target property or intervention is primarily model-internal rather than systems-level.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify sampling procedures, survey questions, or how representative the 26 domains are.
It does not identify which systems-level designs address reliability or provide outcome measures for deployment success.
